solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I don't know bishop in drink, okay

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that other word

blocks.note: 'pass' is what you say in a quiz when you don't know the answer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs about a clergyman having a drink and says it's fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop goes inside the drink, and the quiz-show answer goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passable is adequate, just about acceptable, which is what okay means as an adjective.

clue.text: Travelling up mountain track, perhaps

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the following letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A walker heading up a mountain path.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'track' is itself what the answer names, which is why 'perhaps' follows it: the whole clue both shuffles and points to its own punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma, like the one printed in the clue, is an example of a punctuation mark.

clue.text: Fraud finally destroyed yours truly? Oh, that's awful!

indicators.note: its final letter destroyed means the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a sham is a fraud, a fake
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A fraud has at last ruined the speaker, who exclaims in dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'Shame!' expresses dismay or regret, as 'Oh, that's awful!' does.

clue.text: New IT update for facility

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh computer system upgrade has been rolled out at the facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' looks like a building but here means natural skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility for something is a natural talent for it, which is what aptitude means.

clue.text: French department learning about head of interior

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word surrounds the letter
the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: lore is learning, knowledge
the first letter of interior

explanation.surface: A French government ministry learns about its head of the interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Loire is one of France's administrative departments, named after the river.

clue.text: American beer had befuddled one supposedly enlightened

indicators.note: befuddled means confused and muddled, so the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

blocks.note: Budweiser, a US beer, is known as Bud
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An American beer has left someone muddled, though they think they've reached enlightenment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddha is the title given to an enlightened teacher in Buddhism, the founder of that faith.

clue.text: Politician's anger with posh Lord's official?

blocks.note: U means upper-class
an MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An MP is furious with an upper-class lord's civil servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground, not a peer; 'posh' supplies the first letter though it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire is the official who rules on play in a cricket match, such as one at Lord's.

clue.text: Aberrant mad and racist histrionics

indicators.note: aberrant means straying from the normal, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deranged bigot putting on an overblown display.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatics means exaggerated, theatrical behaviour, which is what histrionics are.

clue.text: Governments reshuffling amid transitions

indicators.note: reshuffling a pack puts the cards in a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Governments carry out cabinet reshuffles during handovers of power.
explanation.definitionFit: An administration is the government of the day, especially in the US sense of a presidency.

clue.text: Soldiers might be prepared before one goes off

definitions.text: Soldiers might be prepared before one goes off

blocks.clueFragment: Soldiers might be prepared before one goes off
blocks.note: surface reading: troops get ready before a bomb or gun goes off
setter's reading: soldiers are strips of toast for dipping into a boiled egg, made ready before the kitchen device rings

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are fingers of buttered toast served with a soft-boiled egg; the device in question rings when the egg is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen timer for boiling eggs goes off when cooking time is up, the cue to serve the toast.

clue.text: New man cutting top of lip in close shave

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only that letter of the following word is wanted
cutting here means removing, so that letter is taken out of the word before it

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
an earthling is a human being, a man as a species
the first letter of lip

explanation.surface: A new man cuts himself shaving near his upper lip, a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: An earthling is any human, so 'man' here means mankind rather than a male. 'Close shave' sounds literal but is the idiom for a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing and a close shave are both idioms for a narrow escape from disaster.

clue.text: Song of soprano that nut producer picks up

indicators.note: to pick something up is to take it in hand, so the tree holds the other letter inside it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
palm trees, such as the coconut palm, produce nuts

explanation.surface: A soprano's song seems to be picked up by some nut-bearing tree, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Banker head of redundancy put up in temporary digs?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so just that one is used
someone put up in lodgings is housed inside them, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: the first letter of redundancy
digs are lodgings, and a tent is a temporary place to stay

explanation.surface: A bank employee facing redundancy has been put up in temporary accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like a person working at a bank, but in crosswords it is something with banks: a river. The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so the crossword sense of 'banker' is a river, and the Trent is one.

clue.text: Flirt with nurse I natter about

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to flirting with a nurse while chatting with her.
explanation.walkthrough: EN, an enrolled nurse, is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain an idea is to consider it lightly, just as to flirt with an idea is to toy with it.

clue.text: Decide a map needs altering for military adviser

indicators.note: something that needs altering must be changed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer must decide whether the campaign map needs changing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer who assists and advises a senior commander.

clue.text: Hot chap doing Rome with a bad temperature

indicators.note: doing something over means reworking it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A handsome man doing the sights of Rome while running a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is an attractive man, and 'hot' is slang for sexually attractive.

clue.text: Give a hand to break up upset cobblers

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word is flipped and read the other way

blocks.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them
to part is to separate, break up

explanation.surface: Someone helps to separate quarrelling shoemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' looks like shoemakers, but it is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap and the British slang 'cobblers' both mean rubbish or nonsense talk.

clue.text: Fail to understand one teaching classes

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... the point is not to grasp it
second meaning: pupils call a female teacher ...

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a pupil not following the lesson; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss a joke is to not get it, and Miss is the form of address for a schoolteacher.

clue.text: Party in possibly automatic Golf tailed guard

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so this piece sits within the others
tailed means followed at the end, so this letter comes after the timepiece

blocks.note: an automatic is one kind of watch, a self-winding one
a do is a party
Golf is G in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A party arrives in what may be an automatic car, with a golf buggy trailing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Automatic' suggests a car, but an automatic is also a self-winding timepiece; the party sits between it and the letter that tails it.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a dog kept to guard property, and by extension any guardian.

clue.text: One costly, but ultimately lacking, plan

indicators.note: lacking its ultimate letter means the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A dear plan that, in the end, fails to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a scheme or proposal, the same as a plan.

clue.text: Horror story provided by Don King's stylist?

blocks.note: first meaning: a frightening tale that makes your hair stand on end
second, playful meaning: Don King, the boxing promoter, was famous for his upright shock of hair, so whoever styled it lifted hair

explanation.walkthrough: Don King was an American boxing promoter whose hair stood straight up; the question mark marks the whimsical second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying story is a hair-raiser because fear makes the hair rise, and King's stylist literally raised hair.

clue.text: Finish cut on black, short hair all at once

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word loses its last letter
short means lacking the end, so the word is trimmed

blocks.note: the end is the finish
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: Finishing a cut on someone's dark, short hair all in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is French for 'as a whole', meaning all together or all at once.

clue.text: Knight tyrannised after daughter's gone and proposed

indicators.note: once something has gone it is no longer there, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight
to tyrannise is to dominate
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A knight who bullied people is put forward for something after his daughter leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the knight in front: N comes before the reduced word.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to propose them as a candidate.

clue.text: Object veterinarian used to restrain bird

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the bird ends up held inside

blocks.note: a vet is a doctor, abbreviated DR
the emu is a large flightless bird

explanation.surface: A vet holding down a bird that resists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb, to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, so it means to object.

clue.text: Yearn to have a partner, in practice?

blocks.note: first meaning: to desire something, often another's
second, punning meaning: a ... would be a fellow vet in a veterinary practice

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CO-VET: CO- means joint, and a vet works in a practice, so a partner in it is a co-vet.
explanation.definitionFit: Covet means to desire eagerly, and as a made-up noun it is a joint veterinary surgeon.

clue.text: Cost of treasure

blocks.note: first meaning: the price or worth of something
second meaning: to prize or cherish something

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the price of a hoard, but 'treasure' is the verb to cherish.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means monetary worth, and as a verb it means to hold dear.

clue.text: A large group of people going around island

indicators.note: going around means turning back on itself, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a lot is a group or set of people

explanation.surface: A big crowd of tourists making their way round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island surrounding a lagoon.

clue.text: One plated molar lad cracked around lunchtime?

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so the letters are scrambled
around means the scrambled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
one o'clock is a typical lunchtime, and I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boy's crowned molar cracks around lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One plated' sounds like a dental crown, but it means a creature with armour plates. The question mark flags lunchtime as one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is a burrowing mammal covered in bony protective plates.

clue.text: Equipment associated with school camp

blocks.note: kit is equipment or gear
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: Gear linked with a school camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like a tented site but here is the adjective for showy, overdone style.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch and camp both describe taste that is garish or exaggerated, enjoyed ironically.

clue.text: Advance publicity awful types ultimately diss

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: PR is public relations, publicity
ogres are monstrous, horrible people
the last letter of diss

explanation.surface: Pre-release publicity that horrible critics end up insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance publicity' reads as one phrase, but 'Advance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress means forward movement, an advance, as noun or verb.
